subtopics.title: Why the State Steps In — and With What

questions.question: The state intervenes in markets because:
options: Price rationing can be intolerable for essentials, externalities go uncharged, harmful goods are overconsumed and incomes are unequal

questions.question: Indirect taxes are:
options: Taxes levied on goods and services — VAT, excise duties, the fuel levy — raising revenue AND changing behaviour

questions.question: A subsidy is:
options: The tax in reverse — the state pays part of the cost, making the good cheaper than the market alone would

questions.question: Welfare instruments — grants, public healthcare, no-fee schools — work by:
options: BYPASSING prices — direct provision and transfers placing buying power or services where income failed

subtopics.title: Taxes and Subsidies on the Diagram

questions.question: An indirect tax shifts:
options: The SUPPLY curve LEFTWARD — sellers need a higher price per unit to offer what they offered before
Nothing — only the price label changes

questions.question: After the tax, the burden typically:
options: SPLITS — price rises by less than the full tax, so buyers pay part and sellers absorb part

questions.question: A subsidy's diagram consequences are:
options: Supply left, price up, quantity down
Supply RIGHT — equilibrium price LOWER, quantity HIGHER (cheaper bus rides, more riders)

questions.question: One honest cost of each instrument:
options: Taxes and subsidies have no costs
A tax set too high breeds smuggling; a subsidy must be funded from taxation elsewhere and can be captured by producers

questions.question: A maximum price is only effective (binding) when set:
options: BELOW the equilibrium price — to make an essential affordable

questions.question: The ceiling's permanent consequence is:
options: A surplus the state must buy
A SHORTAGE — quantity demanded exceeds supplied, and the price is legally forbidden from rising to clear it

questions.question: With price rationing broken, the good is rationed instead by:
options: Queues, first-come-first-served, sellers' favourites and per-customer limits

questions.question: The black market arises because:
options: The shortage's pressure leaks into illegal sales above the ceiling — the desperate paying more than the free market price would ever have been

subtopics.title: Minimum Prices and the Minimum Wage — the Floor

questions.question: A minimum price is set:
options: ABOVE equilibrium, to protect sellers' incomes — historically common for farm produce

questions.question: The floor's consequence is:
options: A SURPLUS — supplied exceeds demanded, and the state typically must buy, store or export the unsold stock
A black market below cost only

questions.question: The minimum wage's mechanical diagram prediction is:
options: More jobs at higher pay for everyone
More labour offered, less demanded — a surplus of labour: unemployment pressure

questions.question: The mature verdict on the minimum wage is:
options: The dignity argument settles it for
A trade-off between protecting the employed and risking the excluded — its actual size an empirical question, measured country by country

questions.question: The referee's four whistles are:
options: Make it dearer (tax), make it cheaper (subsidy), fix the score (price controls), skip the game (welfare)

questions.question: The cigarette tax does "two jobs with one whistle":
options: COLLECTS revenue AND DISCOURAGES smoking through the higher price
Raises and lowers prices at once

questions.question: The referee steps in because the game's natural rule — whoever can pay, plays — is:
options: Sometimes a rule society won't accept for bread, medicine or a working wage

subtopics.title: Ceilings Make Queues, Floors Make Piles

questions.question: Under the bread ceiling, the shelves empty because:
options: At the capped price baking barely pays — many wanting, few baking
The state buys all the bread

questions.question: The cheap bread goes to:
options: Whoever queued from 5 a.m., knows the baker — or pays double in the alley

questions.question: Under the maize floor, the silos overflow because:
options: Buyers buy more at the dear price
Farmers plant everything at the rewarding price while buyers take less — and the price may not fall to clear it

questions.question: The memory trick is:
options: Ceilings make piles; floors make queues
QUEUES under ceilings (pushed low, below equilibrium); PILES on floors (raised high, above equilibrium)

subtopics.title: The Wage Floor at the Factory Gate

questions.question: Truth one of the wage floor:
options: For everyone employed at the floor — rent paid, children fed, dignity restored, wages spent back into the neighbourhood's circle

questions.question: Truth two of the wage floor:
options: Some firms hire fewer hands — and the squeezed-out-first are the youngest and least skilled; some work slips off the books

questions.question: "Possibly BOTH, about different people" answers:
options: The aunt-versus-cousin argument — the wage can save one family while pricing out another; the balance is measured, not shouted

questions.question: The three-question habit for any intervention:
options: Who proposed it, who opposed it, who won?
How much, how long, how often?
Is it left, right or centre?
What was it FOR, what does the diagram predict, and what ELSE follows?
